open_points.subject: one-home rule during service migration
open_points.text: “no other service keeps a customer record or a copy of its values” conflicts with “Until each has, the governance's records of processing list the copies that remain”
open_points.question: Is the one-home rule an immediate invariant of production, or a target invariant that temporarily permits the existing named service copies after production starts?
options: Immediate invariant: dependent services must remove their copies before production starts
Target invariant: existing copies may remain temporarily when individually recorded in governance
Apply the invariant only to copies created or refreshed after production starts
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a target invariant with only the explicitly recorded transitional copies permitted.

open_points.subject: consumer snapshot display name
open_points.text: “A consumer's kept snapshot holds identity — id, display name, status, `customer_ref` — never a personal value” conflicts with “Registry cannot tell a person's name from any other word, so the agent projection leaves out the project's display name”
open_points.question: May a consumer persist `display name` when it can contain a person's name, or must persisted snapshots omit it unless some concrete rule makes it non-personal?
options: Persist display name unconditionally as identity
Omit display name from every persisted consumer snapshot
Permit it only for specifically named consumers or validated non-personal names
open_points.default_guess: Omit display name from persisted snapshots because Registry cannot establish that it is non-personal.

open_points.subject: object identifying characteristics under the one-home rule
open_points.text: “the object's address and identifying characteristics are `personal_data`” but R0-80 says only “the object's address” is held only by Registry
open_points.question: Does the prohibition on copies outside Registry cover all object identifying characteristics as well as the address?
options: All object fields classified `personal_data` follow the one-home rule
Only the address follows the one-home rule
The specification must enumerate which characteristics may be copied
open_points.default_guess: Apply the one-home rule to every object field classified `personal_data`.

open_points.subject: unauthenticated sign-in surface
open_points.text: “Every request on either is authenticated; anything not authenticated is refused” conflicts with the owner's need to “sign in to the owner interface with the owner credential”
open_points.question: Which owner-interface requests, if any, may be answered before an owner session exists so that sign-in can occur?
options: The sign-in form and credential submission are the only unauthenticated exceptions
Authentication occurs outside Registry before any Registry request
Even the sign-in response requires a separate pre-existing credential mechanism
open_points.default_guess: Allow only the sign-in form and credential submission without an existing session, while authenticating the submitted owner credential.

open_points.subject: customer erasure contents
open_points.text: The action says “name, phone, e-mail and language are gone,” while R0-67 says the Customer “keeps its identity and the fact that it was erased” and R0-80 adds kind, tax id and legal name to the record
open_points.question: When customer data is erased, are kind, tax id and legal name also removed, or do any of them survive?
options: Remove every field except `customer_ref` and the erased fact
Remove contact fields but retain kind and fiscal data
Remove all personal fields but retain non-personal kind
open_points.default_guess: Keep only `customer_ref` and the erased fact, removing kind and all contact and fiscal values.

open_points.subject: restriction and fiscal-data use
open_points.text: R0-59 says “A restriction ... covers the customer's contact data,” but “read a customer's billing data” refuses “a restricted customer”
open_points.question: Does restriction block use of fiscal billing data too, or only contact data?
options: It blocks both contact and fiscal data reads
It blocks contact data only, so billing data remains readable
The owner chooses separate restrictions for contact and fiscal data
open_points.default_guess: Honor the explicit billing-action failure and block fiscal-data reads while the customer is restricted.

open_points.subject: missing optional billing fields
open_points.text: Fiscal data is recorded only “when given,” but billing-data output promises “tax id and legal name” without saying what happens when either is absent
open_points.question: What observable result occurs when PresuPro requests billing data for a customer whose tax id or legal name was never recorded?
options: Refuse the read as incomplete billing data
Return the absent fields as null or omitted
Return the available fields and a completeness indicator
open_points.default_guess: Refuse with a specific incomplete-billing-data failure so a document is not issued with guessed values.

open_points.subject: person name returned as billing data
open_points.text: “for a person, the full name as on the document” does not say whether that value comes from the mandatory customer name or the optional fiscal legal name
open_points.question: Which stored field supplies a person's full name to the billing-data operation, and may the operation disclose the ordinary customer name despite the rule that contact data reaches the owner alone?
options: Use fiscal `legal_name` and refuse if absent
Use fiscal `legal_name`, falling back to the customer name
Always use the customer name as the person's billing name
open_points.default_guess: Use fiscal `legal_name` and refuse if it is absent, preserving the contact-data boundary.

open_points.subject: billing read purpose limitation
open_points.text: “today PresuPro, when it issues a document” does not say whether Registry verifies that purpose or merely trusts PresuPro's use of the returned values
open_points.question: Is document issuance an enforceable precondition visible to Registry, or is PresuPro trusted contractually to call the operation only for that purpose?
options: Registry trusts the authenticated PresuPro service to enforce the purpose
The request must identify the document being issued
Registry creates or records an issuance authorization before returning billing data
open_points.default_guess: Treat PresuPro as a trusted service whose contract, rather than Registry runtime state, enforces the stated purpose.

open_points.subject: projects included in the one-time import
open_points.text: R0-79 says “the owner picks any of its projects” and then says “the owner's choice ... is” the two named projects
open_points.question: Is the import input fixed to exactly the two named project ids, or may the owner choose a different subset from the VPS when performing the import?
options: Exactly the two named projects are the accepted import set
The two names record a current intention but the owner may choose any subset at import time
The two named projects are mandatory and additional VPS projects may also be selected
open_points.default_guess: Accept exactly the two named project ids because the decision records the owner's specific migration choice.

open_points.subject: migration export containing personal data
open_points.text: “The owner exports the chosen source and uploads the export through the owner interface” creates a copy of personal data not covered by the document or Client Portal exceptions to “no other service keeps ... a copy”
open_points.question: Where may the migration export exist, who may access it, and what observable event removes it after success or abandonment?
options: A transient owner-controlled encrypted file deleted after successful import
A retained migration record governed as another explicit copy
A direct upload stream that is never persisted outside source and Registry
open_points.default_guess: Use a transient owner-controlled encrypted export and require its deletion after the successful import or an abandoned attempt.

open_points.subject: anonymised projects retaining pointer values
open_points.text: An anonymisation “keeps its id, status and artifact pointers and nothing else,” while R0-68 says pointer values are not inspected and a violating value “does reach the agent”; R0-71 nevertheless says the anonymised project “holds no personal value”
open_points.question: How can anonymisation guarantee that no personal or re-identifying value remains when `uri` or `payload_ref` is retained without inspection?
options: Anonymisation removes or redacts pointer values while retaining non-identifying pointer metadata
The owner must attest that retained pointers are non-identifying before anonymisation succeeds
The no-personal-value statement is only a governance assertion and not a Registry guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Require an owner attestation that the retained pointers are non-identifying before anonymisation is accepted.

open_points.subject: writer of agent-created room names
open_points.text: The action allows “Cabinet Kernel for the agent” to add a room with “the given name,” while R0-68 says “the owner names rooms without names or addresses of people”
open_points.question: Who supplies the room name when an agent adds a room, and does the no-person-or-address naming rule bind agent-written room names?
options: The agent supplies the name and is bound by the same writer rule
Only the owner may supply names, so the agent cannot actually create a named room
Kernel substitutes an owner-approved or generated non-personal name
open_points.default_guess: Let the agent supply the name and state that R0-68's writer rule binds every room-name writer, including the agent through Kernel.

open_points.subject: agent-session access version
open_points.text: “the access version” is returned, but no text says which grants, revocations, active-project changes, pending-request changes or project erasures advance it
open_points.question: Which events change a session's access version, and does replacing or clearing a pending request count?
options: Every mutation of the session record advances it
Only changes to granted projects or the active project advance it
Only grant and revoke operations advance it
open_points.default_guess: Advance it on every session-access mutation, including grant, revoke, active-project change, pending-request replacement or clearing, and removal caused by project erasure.
